title: Customer integration weekly catchup - 2027-01-05
body:
Weekly sync notes — Solutions Eng + ProServices (catchup, fast-format)
Date: 2027-01-05
Facilitator: Claire Nguyen
Attendees: Claire, Ethan, María, Samir, Lina, + TLS from CustomerOps (joined for first 20m)
Duration: 30m

Summary (TL;DR):
- Two customers moving toward limited canary: Veridian (API + embedding pipeline) and Tidewater (dedicated, batch inference).
- Biggest open risks: SSO certificate issues for Tidewater, schema mismatch for Veridian analytics payload, and incomplete test corpus for privacy-regression checks.
- Action focus this week: finalize canary runbook, lock dedicated capacity slots with infra, and get legal signoff for data residency notes.

Customer statuses (concise):
1) Veridian (health: at-risk -> stabilizing)
   - Current step: schema mapping for analytics payload (events_v2) failing 12% of requests in staging.
   - Recent work: María implemented a lenient parser fallback; reduced errors to ~5% but causes a small amount of token misalignment for downstream metrics.
   - Blocker: product wants exact parity on metrics. Need sample of 1,000 golden events from Veridian to root-cause.
   - Next: Claire to request golden set by EOD 2027-01-07; Samir to run KV-cache debug profile once golden set available.
   - Target canary start: 2027-01-14 (conditional on golden-set + infra slot).

2) Tidewater (health: blocked)
   - Current step: private/dedicated rollout planning. Dedicated pool configured but not provisioned due to pending SSO cert and network egress rules.
   - Blocker: Customer SSO cert expired in their IdP, security team will not approve until new cert provided + test SSO handshake. Estimated delay 5-7 business days.
   - Mitigation: Offer temporary hosted route with strict isolation and audit logs; customer evaluating.
   - Action: Ethan to draft temporary hosted SLA and audit checklist (due 2027-01-08). Lina to run infra preflight for dedicated pool (due 2027-01-09).

3) BlueSpruce (health: green -> monitoring)
   - On production for 3 weeks; token-cost slightly above estimate due to long-context prompts. Optimize recommendation: enable prefix caching + dynamic batching for their top 3 heavy routes.
   - Action: Samir to deploy batching knobs to their route (A/B) for 48h starting 2027-01-10. Monitoring annotated in Console dashboard.

Operational notes / decisions made:
- Canary runbook: agreed to single-customer canary for 48h, 0.5% traffic ramp, immediate rollback on any schema regression or >1% client error increase. Claire to finalize runbook and circulate by 2027-01-06.
- Capacity reservation: we committed to reserve 2x A100-equivalent slots for dedicated early ramp customers for the next 4 weeks; finance notified for provisional billing.
- Observability: add a short-lived trace tag `canary=veridian-jan14` and capture per-token latency histogram for first 1000 requests. María owns instrumentation (due 2027-01-13).

Open blockers (top 5):
- SSO cert (Tidewater) — owner: Tidewater Security (external) / internal owner: Ethan — ETA: 2027-01-12
- Golden event sample (Veridian) — owner: Veridian analytics / internal owner: Claire — ETA: 2027-01-07
- Privacy test corpus incomplete — owner: Legal & Privacy / internal owner: Lina — ETA: 2027-01-11
- Infra slot provisioning queued (cloud quotas) — owner: Infra (Ali) / internal owner: Lina — ETA: 2027-01-09
- Regression test flakiness on long-context (BlueSpruce) — owner: Samir — ETA: 2027-01-10

Action items (owners + due):
- Claire: finalize canary runbook + distribution list (2027-01-06) [PRIORITY]
- Ethan: draft temporary hosted SLA and audit checklist for Tidewater (2027-01-08)
- Samir: run KV-cache debug profile for Veridian once golden set available (2027-01-08)
- María: add `canary=veridian-jan14` tracing tags & per-token histograms (2027-01-13)
- Lina: infra preflight for dedicated pool + confirm cloud quota (2027-01-09)
- Legal/Privacy: deliver redacted test corpus for privacy regression (2027-01-11)

Meeting notes (raw snippets / context):
- María: “lenient parser is a temporary band-aid — we still need golden events. We see field-ordering issues from their serializer.”
- Samir: “KV cache appears to mis-index when events have inconsistent metadata keys; I can reproduce with 200 synthetic events.”
- Ethan: “If SSO cert lag continues, offer hosted with strict network locks; get finance buy-in on provisional credits.”

Risks (short matrix):
- Customer churn risk: Medium if Veridian cannot get parity in metrics.
- Security risk: Low-to-medium for temporary hosted route; mitigations in place (audit logs + IP allowlist).
- Schedule drift: High if SSO cert not renewed within 7 business days.

Notes to self / team tips (informal):
- Keep runbook minimal — checklist steps are what we will execute during the canary, not the background history.
- Avoid unbounded retries in the parser fallback — add a metric 'fallback_invocations' so product can decide trade-offs.

Next sync: 2027-01-12 (same channel). If any of the top blockers clears before then, ping #se-proservices-live with updates.

Appendix (quick numbers):
- Reserved capacity: 2x A100-equivalent (baseline), + 1 burst slot (shared)
- Current staging error rate (Veridian): 5% (after lenient parser), target <1%
- BlueSpruce production 95p latency: 220ms (token-level), target <200ms after batching

Attachments referenced: runbook draft (link in linked_artifacts), terraform preflight plan (PR linked), privacy corpus checklist (confluence).

End of notes.
